hero.title: Technology that turns real challenges into solutions
hero.text: We develop digital solutions that connect technology, innovation, and real-world needs. Our current project, NitrusLeaf, applies Artificial Intelligence to the analysis of mandarin leaves.

problem.title:
A challenge in citrus farming
in Vale do Ribeira
problem.paragraph1: Identifying nutritional deficiencies in citrus leaves can be difficult when symptoms are subtle and resemble other visual changes. In the field, this assessment often depends on technical experience and a careful examination of the leaf.
problem.paragraph2: During field research carried out in Vale do Ribeira, cases related to manganese deficiency were observed in mandarin leaves, highlighting the need for tools that can support the preliminary analysis of these changes.

cards.title: Confusion with Greening
cards.subtitle: Similar symptoms, different causes
cards.description: Changes caused by nutritional deficiencies can show visual patterns similar to other conditions such as Greening, making quick identification through observation alone difficult.

cards.title: Field analysis
cards.subtitle: Information needs to be accessible
cards.description: Growers need information that can support the initial identification of changes in the plant without relying exclusively on an immediate specialized assessment.

cards.title: Need for technical support
cards.subtitle: Technology as a support tool
cards.description: Immediate access to specialized knowledge isn't always available. The use of Artificial Intelligence can serve as a complementary tool to support visual analysis.

project.name: NitrusLeaf
project.subtitle: Smart classification of mandarin leaves through Artificial Intelligence
project.description: A mobile app developed to classify images of Citrus reticulata leaves into two categories: manganese deficiency and healthy leaf. The solution uses computer vision and a Convolutional Neural Network to perform a preliminary analysis directly from a phone.

header.title: How we built it
header.subtitle: From field research to classification through Artificial Intelligence

research.title: Research and problem definition
research.subtitle: User Research
objectives: Understand the difficulties related to identifying changes in leaves
Learn about the needs of growers and professionals involved in citrus farming
Identify opportunities for applying technology in an agricultural context

personas.name: João
personas.description: A grower who needs a simple, fast tool to support the preliminary identification of changes in leaves, without relying on complex processes.

personas.name: Ana
personas.description: A professional who can use an image classification tool to support the observation and monitoring of leaf conditions.

fieldCollection.title: Data collection
fieldCollection.subtitle: Field Research
paragraphs: We conducted field research on mandarin-growing properties in Vale do Ribeira, including Sítio São Miguel, in Pariquera-Açu/SP.
During this stage, real growing conditions were observed and images of Citrus reticulata leaves were collected to build the dataset used in developing the model.
checklist: Different conditions and stages of deficiency

preprocessing.title: Preprocessing and data augmentation
preprocessing.subtitle: Image standardization
paragraphs: Images went through automatic orientation correction and were resized to 224 × 224 pixels, using proportional scaling with border padding to preserve their visual characteristics.
During training, data augmentation techniques were applied exclusively to the training set, creating synthetic variations to broaden the diversity of images used by the model.
checklist: Variations in saturation, brightness, and exposure

training.title: Model training
training.subtitle: Convolutional Neural Network
paragraphs: We built a Convolutional Neural Network with three convolutional blocks, using 32, 64, and 128 filters to extract visual features from the leaves at different levels of complexity.
The model uses a dense layer with 512 neurons and 50% Dropout. Training was performed with the Adam optimizer, binary crossentropy loss function, and Early Stopping with a patience of 10 epochs.
checklist: Early Stopping to select the best-performing model

validation.title: Validation
validation.subtitle: Model evaluation
paragraphs: After training, the model was evaluated using a test set of 25 images that were not used during training or validation.
The model achieved 95.97% accuracy on the test set, classifying images between the manganese deficiency and healthy leaf categories.

prototype.title: Mobile app
prototype.subtitle: Working prototype
paragraphs: We built a mobile app capable of receiving an image of a Citrus reticulata leaf and using the AI model to classify it as either manganese deficiency or healthy leaf.
The solution was designed to offer a fast, accessible preliminary analysis directly from a phone, using a photo of the leaf as input.
checklist: Classification between manganese deficiency and healthy leaf
Preliminary analysis directly from the phone

about.title: About us
about.intro: Vitalliz is the team responsible for developing NitrusLeaf, created as part of the Integrating Project for the Multiplatform Software Development program at <strongFatec>Fatec Registro</strongFatec>. Our purpose is to bring together technology, innovation, and knowledge to turn real challenges into accessible digital solutions, with attention to the needs of the regional agricultural context and to <strongOds>UN SDG 2</strongOds> (Zero Hunger and Sustainable Agriculture).
